transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (CISO, Hightower), Marco Reyes (Head of Platform), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Tom Ellis (PM)

Summary (auto): Discussed security posture requirements for potential Redwood deployment. Deep dive on SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Next steps agreed.

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. Quick round and objective - we're here to walk through Redwood's security posture and answer any specific questions about hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments.
[00:18] Karen Liu: Thanks Alex, hi all. Our main ask is we need to validate compliance artefacts and how your controls map to our assessment. SOC2 is table stakes, ISO is desirable. Also very interested in SSO and fine grained RBAC and logs, we have auditors in three weeks so timeline's a bit tight.
[00:33] Samir Patel: Totally, we'll go through what we have and then dig into any network or KMS questions. High level first: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem) — each has different tradeoffs on isolation and control.
[00:50] Marco Reyes: Quick clarif, when you say Private VPC is the control plane still managed by Redwood? We prefer customer-managed control plane for any regulated workloads.
[01:05] Priya Shah: Good question. For Private we offer an option for a customer-managed control plane, or a private control plane hosted in your cloud account. On-prem is available as a packaged deployment. For the VPC option, networking and peering are set up in your account and you control the subnets and routing.
[01:25] Aisha Khan: And KMS? Our policy requires keys to be in our KMS, no exceptions.
[01:33] Samir Patel: We support BYOK via customer KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in supported cloud KMSs (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) — there's an option to rotate keys on a schedule.
[01:50] Tom Ellis: Is there HSM-backed key use for higher assurance?
[01:54] Priya Shah: Yes, HSM-backed keys are supported through AWS CloudHSM or equivalent via KMS integration; we have customers using that for higher assurance.
[02:08] Karen Liu: Can you show where audit logs live and how we access them? We need immutable logs for certain admin activities.
[02:16] Samir Patel: Audit logs are streamable to your logging endpoint — we can push to S3/GCS/Azure Blob, or forward to SIEMs via syslog/forwarder. For Dedicated and Private deployments logs can be centralized in your account so you retain custody. The logs include request metadata, auth events, admin actions, and key lifecycle events.
[02:37] Karen Liu: How granular are the RBAC roles? We need separation between dev, prod, and auditors with very limited rights.
[02:45] Alex Morgan: We have role templates plus custom roles. Roles cover route-level permission, model-level access, ability to view usage/cost, and admin actions like key rotation or deployment rollouts. There's SAML/SCIM integrations for group sync so you can map your Okta/IdP groups to Redwood roles.
[03:05] Marco Reyes: Okta is our IdP. Does your SSO support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:11] Samir Patel: Yes SAML 2.0 for SSO, and SCIM 2.0 for user/group provisioning. We also support OIDC for app-level flows. There can be some minor mapping quirks — sometimes attributes named differently — but we generally work through that with a short mapping doc.
[03:30] Karen Liu: Auditors will want evidence of separation of duties and role reviews — do you keep snapshots of role assignments?
[03:37] Priya Shah: We keep an audit trail of role assignments and changes; for Hosted customers we provide exports of role-change events. For Dedicated/Private those logs are pushed to the customer's log destination so you can retain them for your audit retention period.
[03:52] Tom Ellis: Data retention - we have a max retention of 90 days for certain PII, some logs can be retained longer. How does Redwood handle retention of request/response data and embeddings?
[04:03] Samir Patel: By default Hosted API session data isn't retained beyond operational logs but we do offer configurable retention and deletion policies. For Dedicated and Private you control retention — you can set TTLs on stored artifacts or purge KV caches. We also have data deletion APIs and an erasure process that is documented. Note: embeddings and models derived from data require explicit opt-in storage.
[04:28] Karen Liu: Are model responses ever used to train Redwood models? That's a hard no from compliance side unless data is explicitly opted-in.
[04:35] Alex Morgan: Understood — Redwood's Hosted product has an enterprise setting to opt out of any training/analytics. We do not train public models on customer data unless explicit agreement. For Dedicated/Private there is no passthrough to shared training. We'll include the policy language in the pack.
[04:53] Marco Reyes: Network controls - do you support private peering and IP allow lists? We want to lock traffic to our VPCs.
[05:01] Priya Shah: Yes, VPC peering, PrivateLink, and IP allow-listing are supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be restricted via IP allow lists and API gateway with TLS mTLS options in front.
[05:16] Karen Liu: Encryption at rest and in transit?
[05:19] Samir Patel: All in-transit is TLS 1.2+/1.3. At rest data and artifacts are encrypted with customer-managed keys where configured. Disk-level encryption and object-level encryption supported for cloud buckets.
[05:32] Karen Liu: What about database backups and snapshots? They need to be encrypted and accessible only to select roles.
[05:39] Samir Patel: Backups are encrypted with the same KMS policies and access is restricted; for Dedicated/Private, backup snapshots live in your account and adhere to your IAM.
[05:52] Tom Ellis: Can we set event alerts for suspicious admin activity?
[05:56] Alex Morgan: Yes, we have event hooks and alerting integrations with PagerDuty/Splunk/Sumo Logic — you can subscribe to admin events and it can trigger workflows.
[06:07] Karen Liu: Is Redwood SOC2 Type II? Can we get the report?
[06:10] Alex Morgan: We are SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certified — I'll share the certs and the SOC2 report under an NDA. We'll drop the compliance pack (link) after this call.
[06:21] Aisha Khan: Small thing on telemetry — we want to ensure PII is redacted before it's included in any logs. Is there automatic redaction?
[06:29] Priya Shah: We provide a PII redaction layer you can enable; by default we don't persist user data in logs, but if you have custom logs or opt-in features we can apply redaction rules or send logs to a processing bucket in your account where you run the redaction.
[06:45] Marco Reyes: Regarding latency-sensitive endpoints, do you provide region-specific deployments and data residency guarantees?
[06:52] Samir Patel: Yes, we have region-based hosts and can pin the model serving to a region; for Private you control the region. We can sign data residency addenda for EU/UK.
[07:05] Karen Liu: For the upcoming audit they'd also like to see change management docs, incident response runbooks, and evidence of DR tests. Do you have that?
[07:15] Alex Morgan: Yes, we'll include change management and incident response summaries in the pack. We run DR tests and can provide high-level evidence and dates. Detailed playbooks are shared under NDA.
[07:29] Tom Ellis: Okay, any constraints on bringing in custom models or quantized variants in Dedicated? We use a mix of open models and a couple of proprietary ones.
[07:38] Samir Patel: Dedicated supports custom models; the runtime supports quantized weights, and we recommend doing an onboarding kernel/benchmark run. For Private on-prem you have full control over model binaries. There are some signing and provenance checks we run for hosted artefacts.
[07:58] Karen Liu: Regarding audit logs again, can we keep a read-only immutable ledger for critical admin actions?
[08:05] Priya Shah: You can push logs to an S3 bucket with object lock enabled for immutability, or to your SIEM where immutability controls exist. We'll help outline a pattern.
[08:19] Aisha Khan: How granular are the logs for inference requests — do you log full inputs/outputs or just metadata?
[08:26] Samir Patel: We log metadata by default (request id, model, token counts, latency); full request/response bodies are opt-in and can be masked or stored in your account only if you enable that.
[08:40] Marco Reyes: For retention we need certain logs for 7 years for financial audits, but access restricted. Can Redwood support different retention windows per log type?
[08:48] Alex Morgan: Yes, retention policies can be configured per-log type and per-destination for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can request longer retention under enterprise plans and have logs exported to their storage with the retention they control.
[09:02] Karen Liu: Are there penetration test reports or a vulnerability disclosure program we can review?
[09:07] Samir Patel: We have pen-test summaries and a vulnerability disclosure / bug bounty program. Full reports are shared under NDA; summaries are in the public repo.
[09:20] Tom Ellis: Onboarding timeline — if we go Dedicated, how long to get a reserved pool up and running?
[09:26] Priya Shah: Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for Dedicated capacity provisioning and network setup, shorter if you have a standard cloud account. Private on-prem depends on infra readiness — could be 4-8 weeks.
[09:40] Karen Liu: For our security team, would prefer a technical deep dive where your SEs validate KMS integration and run a short benchmark with sample traffic.
[09:49] Alex Morgan: Absolutely — Samir and Priya can lead a benchmarking session. We'll propose an agenda: network walkthrough, KMS proof-of-concept, log export proof, and a short 30k-token perf run.
[10:05] Marco Reyes: Perf run — do you have synthetic scripts or we provide traffic?
[10:09] Samir Patel: We have scripts and can adapt to your traffic profile; best to run both so we validate real-case latency and throughput.
[10:18] Karen Liu: About governance — does Redwood provide attestation for patching and software versions for the runtime?
[10:24] Priya Shah: We publish runtime versioning and patch notes. For Dedicated/Private we can provide an attestation of patch windows and installed versions.
[10:34] Tom Ellis: Curious about encryption key rotation — who can rotate and what's the process?
[10:38] Samir Patel: Key rotation is an admin action; you can require dual-approval via RBAC + workflow. For customer-managed KMS rotation happens in your KMS, and Redwood handles re-encryption of objects in a rolling fashion; we log the event.
[10:55] Karen Liu: Any known gaps or things we should be aware of as auditors dig in?
[10:59] Alex Morgan: Nothing substantive; I'll be candid that Hosted customers have less direct control of infrastructure and may need compensating controls for highly regulated workflows — that's where Dedicated or Private shines. We'll call that out explicitly in the pack.
[11:15] Aisha Khan: Operational question — if an operator accidentally pushes PII, how fast can we purge? Is there a guaranteed SLA for erasure?
[11:24] Priya Shah: We have an erasure API which can purge stored artifacts; Typical turnaround depends on the storage location — for Dedicated/Private where data is in your account it's immediate upon request. For Hosted we commit to documented SLAs — we'll include those in the compliance pack.
[11:41] Marco Reyes: Can we get an exemplar key policy for KMS and IAM roles for service accounts?
[11:46] Samir Patel: Yes, Samir will send sample IAM and KMS policies.
[11:51] Karen Liu: Great. For the audit we also need a contact for incident response and a point of escalation.
[11:58] Alex Morgan: That's me at first level, then our infosec lead — I'll include contact details in the follow-up.
[12:07] Tom Ellis: Any blockers on regulatory frameworks like GDPR? Data subject requests?
[12:12] Priya Shah: We support DSAR workflows; for Hosted we provide tools and processes and for Dedicated/Private you manage DSAR handling in your environment.
[12:23] Karen Liu: Ok let's recap next steps.
[12:26] Alex Morgan: Recap: Alex to send SOC2+ISO pack (NDA), pen-test summaries, incident/DR docs; Samir to schedule technical deep dive with KMS and log export tests; Marco to share retention policy and architecture diagram. We'll aim to have the pack by 2027-09-01 and schedule the deep dive for week of 2027-09-05.
[12:46] Karen Liu: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:50] Alex Morgan: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with the links.

References and links mentioned:
- Compliance pack (to be shared): https://redwood.example.com/compliance-pack (NDA)
- Docs: https://redwood.example.com/docs/security (SSO/KMS/RBAC/Audit)
- Benchmark scripts (example): https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/synthetic

End of transcript.
